An OSError while reading an existing ledger is treated like a missing ledger: with no usable backup, _backup_or_empty returns an empty list and the next add/edit/remove writes a fresh ledger over the unreadable file. On POSIX a file whose read bit is denied but whose directory is writable can be replaced, so a permissions or I/O error can silently destroy the ledger. Refuse the write instead of st

shutil.copy2 truncates the existing .bak before writing the new copy. A crash or power loss during this copy leaves a partial backup, destroying the last recoverable version; the ledger itself is still valid until the following replace, but a later corruption then has no usable backup. Copy to a temporary file, fsync it, and replace .bak atomically before replacing the ledger.

findings.message: The distribution version was bumped to 0.2.0, but tally/__init__.py still declares `__version__ = "0.1.0"`. Package metadata and the importable module now report different versions, so consumers and bug reports can disagree about which release they are running. Update the module version in the same change as the next package bump.
